name: Rubber Legs
hook: Knees give out instantly — and your upper body refuses to notice.
description: Elastic knee buckles, sideways rebounds and noodle-walk wobbles below the waist, while the upper body stays calm and composed. Funny in the first frame, and forgiving when motion transfer isn't perfect.

movement.firstSecond: Both knees buckle inward at once and the body drops ~20cm — while hands stay casually in pockets and the face stays deadpan — then springs back up.
movement.signature: The Composed Collapse: a deep inward knee buckle with a perfectly still, unimpressed upper body.

sequence.name: Buckle
sequence.description: Instant inward knee buckle and drop; upper body composed. Spring back.

sequence.name: Rebound
sequence.description: Legs snap outward and the body bounces sideways to one side.

sequence.name: Noodle walk
sequence.description: Two steps with extreme knee wobble, feet flicking outward.

sequence.name: Business as usual
sequence.description: Upper body casually adjusts collar or sleeve while the legs keep wobbling.

sequence.name: Double buckle
sequence.description: Two quick buckles, then straighten sharply to attention.

movement.loopPoint: Ends standing straight with hands in pockets — the same stance the opening buckle starts from.
movement.cameraGuidance: Locked-off camera at hip height, full body in frame with some headroom so the vertical drop reads clearly.
transferConsiderations: Designed to tolerate imperfect transfer: exaggerated leg motion hides minor limb artifacts.
Keep hands visible or clearly in pockets for the whole take — half-hidden hands confuse pose estimation.
Knee buckles should stay above ~90° to avoid self-occlusion of the legs.

recipe.prompt: The person from the photo does a comedic wobbly-legs dance with a calm, composed upper body, in a clean, evenly lit space. Preserve their face, body shape, hair and clothing exactly. Stable camera.

provenance.notes: Original concept created for TREND MACHINE launch. Not derived from any specific existing viral trend.

rights.notes: No music is bundled. Audio is handled separately from movement.
